name: AWM: Agent Workflow Memory
venue: ICML 2025 (Forty-second International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 42nd ICML, ACM DOI 10.5555/3780338.3782875). NOTE: the task metadata listed 'ICLR 2025', but the verified peer-reviewed venue is ICML 2025 (OpenReview id NTAhi2JEEE, ICML 2025 Poster). Preprint: arXiv:2409.07429 (cs.CL), v1 submitted 11 Sep 2024.
authors_affiliation: Zora Zhiruo Wang (Carnegie Mellon University), Jiayuan Mao (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Daniel Fried (Carnegie Mellon University), Graham Neubig (Carnegie Mellon University). Lead author: Zora Zhiruo Wang (CMU).
code_url: https://github.com/zorazrw/agent-workflow-memory (Apache-2.0; ~442 stars; pipelines for both webarena/ and mind2web/).
task_domain: web / decision-making: LM-based web-navigation agents that perceive web observations (accessibility tree on WebArena; filtered HTML / element candidates on Mind2Web) and emit executable actions (click, type, stop, etc.) to complete long-horizon tasks across travel, shopping, social media, software development, content management, and maps.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent sequential decision-making for web navigation. An LM-backbone agent L with a text-based memory M (base memory = built-in action docs such as CLICK/TYPE) solves a task specified by an NL instruction q in an environment with transition function T: at each step t_i, observation o_i is fed to the model to generate action a_i via L(q, M, o_i) -> a_i, executed until STOP or a max-step termination. AWM induces reusable workflows W = {w} from past experiences E = {e} via an induction module I(E) -> W, then augments memory M + W -> M_w to guide subsequent task-solving. Two settings: (1) OFFLINE — when high-quality annotated/canonical training examples are available (Mind2Web cross-task training set), workflows are induced once from training examples beforehand and used frozen at test time; (2) ONLINE / supervision-free — only test queries exist (WebArena, and Mind2Web cross-website/cross-domain); the agent processes test queries in a streaming manner, after each task it judges success with an LM evaluator (Pan et al. 2024 AutoEval) and, if success, induces workflows and appends them to memory for subsequent tasks (continual / streaming growth). Frozen LM backbone (no gradient updates); workflows are text/code injected into the prompt context. AWM is run on a per-website basis (examples grouped by website) to keep the workflow set small and relevant.
what_is_retrieved: workflows (reusable routines / sub-routines induced from past agent trajectories). Each workflow = an NL description d (the high-level goal/summary) + a series of steps (p1, p2, ...) where each step has (1) an NL description of the current environment state, (2) the agent's reasoning, and (3) an executable program action. Example-specific values are abstracted out (e.g., 'dry cat food' -> '{product-name}').
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes (with an offline-induced variant). In the online setting the workflow memory is a growing store the agent continually writes to from its own (evaluator-verified) successful test-time trajectories. In the offline setting the store is induced once from annotated training examples and frozen at test time. Both are agent-induced experience memory, not a static external corpus/KB/API set. Overall: growing/episodic memory (online) or offline-induced experience memory (offline); not a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not a top-k ranking objective. AWM does NOT rank-and-select top-k workflows per query; in the reported main results it injects ALL induced workflows for a given website into the agent memory at once (whole-memory augmentation), and lets the LM selectively attend to/apply relevant ones during generation. Selection is therefore an all-relevant-workflows-as-context scheme (kept small via per-website grouping; ~7.3-7.4 workflows/example), closer to providing the complete useful routine set than a fixed-k recommendation. The paper notes the design 'selectively providing workflows', but selection within context is done by the LM rather than an explicit retriever.
retrieval_unit: workflow-routine: a reusable sub-routine (a frequently re-appearing sub-task such as 'search for a product on Amazon' or 'find a place by its name'), represented as <description, ordered steps> where each step = (NL state description, reasoning, executable program action). Finer-grained than a full task trajectory; example-specific contexts are abstracted away. (In the AWM-AS variant a workflow is wrapped as a callable high-level function/action.)
index_source: Hybrid by setting. OFFLINE: store is offline-induced from the annotated training set (Mind2Web cross-task training examples), built once and frozen. ONLINE: store is online/test-time-induced and grows in a streaming fashion from the agent's own evaluator-verified successful test trajectories (no annotated data). An AWM-off+on integration combining both is also explored (Appendix C). The store is an induced experience/workflow memory, not a pre-existing corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat textual workflow list embedded directly in the agent memory / prompt context (system prompt or auxiliary prompt context). Workflows are segmented (by double-line breaks in the LM output) and stored separately as individual entries; grouped/partitioned by website. No vector index, dependency graph, or learned hierarchy. (Implicit compositional hierarchy emerges because later complex workflows are built on top of earlier simpler ones, e.g., 'get the zip code of a place' reuses 'find a place by its name', but there is no explicit graph structure.)
retriever_type: LLM-as-selector / no explicit retriever. There is no BM25/dense/learned retrieval module: the induced workflows for a website are all placed into context, and the LM itself decides which workflows to use during generation. (The rule-based induction variant uses action-sequence deduplication, not retrieval. The compared baseline Synapse uses dense retrieval of concrete examples, but AWM replaces that with always-in-context abstract workflows.) Closest label: LLM-as-retriever / in-context selection by the generation LM.
retriever_learning_signal: none (no trained retriever). Selection of which workflows to apply is performed implicitly by the frozen generation LM from the workflows present in context; there is no contrastive/LM-feedback/RL/value-based training of a retrieval component. The induction module is a frozen LM prompted to extract sub-routines (LM-based) or a deterministic rule-based dedup procedure; neither is trained. The only learning signal in the loop is the LM evaluator's binary success label gating online write-back (not a retriever-training signal).
query_construction: No explicit query is constructed for retrieval (all workflows for the website are provided in context). For workflow INDUCTION, the 'query' to the induction LM is the concatenation of one or more past experiences (NL instruction q + full action trajectory of (observation, action) steps); offline it concatenates all training examples of a website into a single prompt; online it feeds the single just-completed (evaluator-verified) experience. Induction prompts instruct the LM to extract finer-grained sub-routines and abstract out example-specific values into placeholders (e.g., {product-name}).
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0) for utilization: for each test task the full website workflow memory is provided once at the start and reused across all steps of that episode (no per-step re-query). For induction, the granularity is trajectory/experience-level (whole completed experiences are summarized into sub-routine workflows).
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (per task) for utilization — the workflow memory is provided once at task start and not re-retrieved within the episode. The MEMORY itself is updated/grown on a one-task-at-a-time schedule in the online setting (induce-integrate-utilize loop after each completed test task), but there is no within-episode iterative or uncertainty-triggered retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule. Utilization: workflows are unconditionally included in memory at the start of each task. Memory write/update (online): triggered deterministically after every completed test task, gated by the LM evaluator's binary success judgment (write only if predicted success). Offline: workflows induced once before test time on a fixed schedule. No token-confidence/attention/reflection-token/agent-initiated retrieval trigger.
reranking: None. No reranking stage; all induced website-level workflows are injected and the LM attends to relevant ones during generation.
retrieved_context_refinement: Refinement happens at INDUCTION/WRITE time rather than at retrieval time: the LM induction module distills full trajectories into finer-grained sub-routine workflows, abstracts out example-specific values into placeholders ({product-name}), and segments outputs into separate workflow entries; the rule-based variant deduplicates by action sequence and filters invalid (non-executable) steps. At utilization time the workflows are injected as-is (no per-query rerank/compress/decompose). Optional state-abstraction explorations (Sec 4.3) describe environment states in NL vs filtered HTML, but NL descriptions worked best and HTML augmentation hurt.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation / skill reuse: induced workflows are integrated into the agent's text memory (M + W -> M_w) so the agent generates actions via L(q, M+W, o) -> a, using workflows as in-context guidance / reusable routines. An additional AWM-AS variant promotes workflows to skill reuse by wrapping each workflow into a callable high-level action (e.g., find_place, login) added to the agent's action space, executing a pre-determined sequence of primitive actions when invoked.
planning_integration: retrieve(induce)-then-plan with workflows as in-context guidance: induced workflows are added to memory and used as one-shot, plan-time guidance that conditions a per-step observe-act loop (L(q, M_w, o_i) -> a_i executed by T until STOP). Workflows describe high-level goals + ordered steps that the agent follows/adapts while acting. In the online setting this is interleaved across tasks (plan task t, induce workflow, plan task t+1 with augmented memory). In AWM-AS, workflows become callable macro-actions inside the per-step action loop. No tree search/MCTS; no per-step re-retrieval.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-task for retrieval/memory provisioning (workflows provided once per task) combined with per-step (per-tool-call) acting within the rollout. In the online setting, the induce-integrate-utilize cycle is interleaved at the per-task granularity (after each completed task). Workflow application within an episode is woven into the per-step action generation, but no fresh retrieval occurs per CoT-step or per-token.
retrieved_item_representation: free-text/code workflow: each injected workflow is an NL description d plus an ordered list of steps, each step containing (1) an NL state description (e.g., 'Order {id} is shown'), (2) the agent's NL reasoning, and (3) an executable program action (e.g., stop(), click(id), type(id, text)). Example-specific values are replaced with abstract placeholders ({product-name}, {id}). Explored alternatives: a fully textual (verbalized) workflow format (AWM-text) and HTML-augmented states — code and text forms performed comparably. In AWM-AS the workflow is an executable high-level function.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: reusable workflow / distilled procedural sub-routine: an abstracted, frequently-reused routine with example-specific contexts removed (placeholders) — explicitly NOT a raw full-trajectory exemplar (the paper contrasts this with Synapse's concrete full-example retrieval, attributing AWM's gains to the abstract, reusable nature of workflows that reduces element-selection bias). Sits between a raw trajectory and a high-level skill; described as a common sub-routine / task recipe.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) LM evaluator gating: in the online setting only evaluator-verified successful trajectories are turned into workflows, filtering incorrect experiences before write-back (though imperfect — wrong workflows from mis-judged trajectories can still degrade performance); (2) abstraction of example-specific contexts into placeholders reduces over-fitting/element-selection bias from concrete exemplars; (3) rule-based induction filters invalid (non-executable) actions and deduplicates redundant trajectories; (4) per-website grouping keeps the workflow set small and relevant; (5) the agent is observed to learn to diverge from workflow guidelines when they do not match the current state (though imperfectly — slightly lower Action F1 than MindAct). No retriever-aware contrastive/distractor-aware SFT (frozen LM).
memory_type: workflow memory (procedural / skill-library-like text memory): a continually-built text memory of reusable workflows (routines) augmenting the base action-documentation memory. Combines workflow + procedural-skill characteristics; in AWM-AS workflows additionally act as a callable skill library.
write_back: Yes (online). The system stores newly induced workflows from past (successful) experiences into the agent memory (M^t + {w^t} -> M^{t+1}). In the offline setting write-back occurs once before test time (induced from training examples); in the online setting it occurs continually at test time.
online_growth: Yes (in the online setting). The workflow memory grows during deployment/test-time in a streaming fashion as the agent induces and appends new workflows after each completed (evaluator-verified) test task, creating a snowball/continual-learning effect (e.g., +22.5 points gain over baseline after only tens of WebArena examples). In the offline-only setting the store is frozen after pre-test induction.
write_back_trigger: Online: reflective / on-success-only after each task — after each completed test task an LM evaluator (Pan et al. 2024) outputs a binary success label; only if predicted success (label = 1) is the experience transformed into workflow(s) and appended to memory. Offline: induced once from the annotated training set before test time (a one-time write on a fixed schedule). No failure-triggered or human-validated writes in the main method.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only. Only successful experiences (offline: ground-truth annotated training examples; online: evaluator-judged-correct self-generated trajectories) are converted into workflows and stored. Failed/negative trajectories are NOT stored or retrieved; there are no contrastive success+failure entries or failure-derived corrective rules. (The paper analyzes a workflow-action failure case (book_flight pop-up airports) qualitatively but does not feed failures back as memory.)
memory_evolution_update: Append-only with implicit compositional build-up. New workflows are appended to memory; the agent builds increasingly complex workflows on top of earlier simpler ones (e.g., 'get the zip code of a place' composes/extends 'find a place by its name'), so functionality grows compositionally over time. The paper does not implement explicit dedup-merge/delta-update/refine-overwrite/forget-prune of existing entries during online growth (induction quality metrics report low inter-workflow function overlap ~0.08-0.20, i.e., naturally near-non-overlapping appends). Rule-based induction deduplicates at induction time only.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Workflow selection/use is not a learned or RL-optimized retrieval policy; relevant workflows are chosen implicitly by the frozen generation LM from the in-context workflow set. The only learned/neural decision in the loop is the LM success-evaluator gating online write-back, which is a verification policy, not a retrieval policy. Selection is not a fixed similarity top-k either — it is whole-memory (all website workflows) in-context provisioning.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private workflow memory; workflows are induced and used by the same agent (grouped per website). No cross-agent or cross-framework experience/memory sharing.
benchmarks: WebArena (812 web navigation tasks over 5 self-hosted websites covering e-commerce/shopping, social forum/Reddit, software development/GitLab, content management/CMS, and maps; execution-based functional-correctness evaluation; online setting only). Mind2Web (versatile real-world web navigation with cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain test splits; offline + online settings; element accuracy / action F1 / step SR / task SR metrics). Together 1000+ tasks from 200+ domains.
baselines: WebArena: BrowserGym (Drouin et al. 2024; current SOTA autonomous, both default and accessibility-tree-only BrowserGym_ax-tree), AutoEval/AutoEval-style AutoEval (Pan et al. 2024), the original WebArena agent (Zhou et al. 2024), and SteP (Sodhi et al. 2023; uses 14 human-expert-written workflows). Mind2Web: MindAct (Deng et al. 2023; element-filtering + multi-choice format), Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024; trajectory-as-exemplar retrieval of concrete examples), and CogAgent (referenced). Backbone LLMs: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613, temperature 0) on WebArena and Mind2Web; GPT-3.5-turbo (temperature 0) additionally on Mind2Web; same model used for workflow induction and action generation. Online success evaluator: LM-based evaluator from Pan et al. 2024.
key_metrics: WebArena: task success rate (SR, %) with per-website breakdown, plus average number of steps (efficiency). Mind2Web: element accuracy (Elem Acc / EA), action F1 (AF1), step success rate (Step SR), and whole-task success rate (SR). Workflow-quality intrinsic metrics: number of workflows, coverage, function overlap, utility rate.
headline_result: WebArena: 35.5% overall task success rate with GPT-4 (online AWM), the best published autonomous result — +12.0 absolute points / +51.1% relative over the BrowserGym baseline (23.5%), and +7.6%-7.9% relative over SteP (33.0%) despite SteP using 14 human-written workflows and AWM using no human supervision; AWM also reduces steps (5.9 vs 7.9 for BrowserGym_ax-tree, ~40.8 fewer than AutoEval). Mind2Web cross-task: +24.6% relative step-wise success rate over baseline (e.g., GPT-4 AWM_offline Step SR 45.1 vs MindAct 36.2). Online AWM generalizes by +8.9 to +14.0 absolute step-SR points as train-test distribution gaps widen. (GitHub README states 35.6% SR, matching the rule-based variant AWM_rule = 35.6, LM-based AWM_lm = 35.5.)
ablations: (1) LM-based vs rule-based induction: comparable on WebArena (AWM_rule 35.6 / 6.3 steps vs AWM_lm 35.5 / 5.9 steps) but LM-based clearly better on Mind2Web (AWM_lm Step SR 45.1 / SR 4.8 vs AWM_rule 43.4 / 2.0), showing the abstract finer-grained sub-routine format drives the Mind2Web gain (Sec 4.1, Tables 5-6). (2) Abstract workflows vs concrete examples: vs Synapse (retrieved full examples) AWM gives +5.0 Elem Acc and +4.0 Step SR, attributed to less element-selection bias from abstraction (Sec 3.2.1). (3) Workflow format text vs code (Sec 4.2, Table 7): comparable — AWM_text slightly higher Step SR (45.4 vs 45.1) but lower task SR (3.6 vs 4.8). (4) Environment abstraction (Sec 4.3, Table 8): NL state descriptions > filtered HTML; using both NL+HTML hurts (Step SR 32.9). (5) Workflows in action space AWM-AS (Sec 5, Table 9): +1.3 Step SR (46.4) but same overall SR (3.2); workflow actions invoked in only 18.5% of tasks. (6) Online vs offline on Mind2Web generalization (Table 4): online generalizes better as domain gap widens (cross-domain Step SR online 35.5 vs offline 32.6); offline+online integration (Appendix C) gives intermediate, sub-additive results. (7) Efficient learning (Sec 3.1.2, Fig 5): a steep learning curve within ~40 WebArena map examples. (8) Workflow-quality analysis (Appendix A.3, Table 10): WebArena 7.4 workflows, utility rate 0.94, function overlap 0.08; Mind2Web 7.3 workflows, coverage 0.40, function overlap 0.20, utility rate 0.91.
evaluation_decoupling: Partially. The paper reports intrinsic workflow-quality metrics (number of workflows, coverage, function overlap, utility rate; Appendix A.3 Table 10) separately from end-to-end task metrics, and on Mind2Web reports element accuracy / action F1 as sub-step intrinsic-style measures. However it does NOT report standard ranked-retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) because there is no explicit top-k retriever; workflow effectiveness is assessed mainly via downstream task gains plus the workflow-quality metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. WebArena uses outcome (task success rate) plus efficiency (number of steps). Mind2Web adds intermediate process metrics: per-step Step SR, element accuracy, and action F1, in addition to whole-task SR. Workflow-quality metrics (coverage, utility rate, function overlap) further probe process/memory quality beyond final outcome.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a headline benefit. WebArena: AWM uses ~5.9 steps/task vs 7.9 for BrowserGym_ax-tree (~2.0 fewer) and ~40.8 fewer steps than AutoEval (which adds evaluation+refinement loops), i.e., higher success with shorter trajectories. AWM needs no human-written workflows (vs SteP's 14) and works supervision-free online. Sample efficiency: substantial gains after only ~40 examples (Fig 5). Memory footprint is small: ~7.3-7.4 workflows per website with high utility (0.91-0.94) and low overlap (0.08-0.20). No explicit dollar/latency numbers beyond step counts; online adds one LM evaluator call + one LM induction call per task.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Whole-memory-in-context, budget-controlled by per-website grouping. All workflows induced for a given website (kept small, ~7.3-7.4 per website per the quality analysis) are concatenated into the agent memory/prompt at once rather than selecting a fixed k by similarity; per-website grouping is the explicit mechanism to keep the injected set small and relevant. No fixed-k or reranked-then-truncated retrieval; the generation LM attends to relevant workflows. Greedy decoding (temperature 0) for both GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: partial (workflows provided in context / selected implicitly by the LM, no explicit similarity retriever), Reuse: yes (workflows used as in-context guidance / callable skills to solve new tasks), Revise: partial (no per-case revision of a retrieved workflow at solve time, but workflows are induced/abstracted from experiences and complex ones are composed from simpler ones; the LM may diverge from workflow guidance), Retain: yes (induced workflows are retained in memory, online growth)]. AWM most strongly implements Reuse + Retain, with abstraction/induction at write time; explicit Retrieve and Revise are weak/implicit.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is presented as agent workflow memory / library learning / skill induction, motivated by cognitive-science work on expert routines (Chi et al. 1981/2014). It nonetheless realizes CBR-style Reuse+Retain over abstracted procedural routines rather than concrete cases.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method). In the AWM-AS variant induced workflows are wrapped as callable high-level functions (e.g., login(username,password)) added to the action space, but there is no tool-description indexing/augmentation pipeline.
index_content_separation: No. Each workflow carries both its lightweight NL description and its full step content together in memory; there is no separate lightweight retrievable index pointing to on-demand heavy content (no progressive disclosure / SOP-index-then-content scheme). Workflows are kept compact via per-website grouping and abstraction instead.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no live tool index/MCP/RapidAPI/REST integration; environment interaction is via WebArena/BrowserGym and Mind2Web action APIs and executable program actions).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling). Workflows do exhibit implicit compositional dependency among themselves — complex workflows reuse simpler ones — but this is not modeled as a dependency graph or dependency-aware retrieval.
adaptation_mechanism: LM-prompted induction/abstraction at write time + in-context guidance at solve time. Cases (experiences) are adapted into reusable form by an LM induction module that extracts finer-grained sub-routines and replaces example-specific values with placeholders; at solve time the retrieved workflow is reused as in-context guidance that the LM instantiates to the current task (filling placeholders) and may diverge from when the environment state differs. No execution-feedback-driven per-case revision loop, no critic-guided revision, no RL fine-tuning.
builds_on: Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024; trajectory-as-exemplar retrieval — AWM swaps concrete retrieved examples for abstract workflows) and MindAct/Mind2Web (Deng et al. 2023; element filtering + multi-choice format, reused as the agent backbone on Mind2Web); BrowserGym/WorkArena (Drouin et al. 2024) and WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024) frameworks; LM-based library-learning / skill-induction lineage (LATM/Cai et al. 2023, TroVE Wang et al. 2024c, Voyager Wang et al. 2023a skill library) and rule-based program library learning (DreamCoder/Ellis et al. 2023, Stitch/Bowers et al. 2023, LILO/Grand et al. 2023); AutoEval (Pan et al. 2024) LM success evaluator used to gate online write-back; SteP/HEAP (Sodhi et al. 2023) human-written workflows compared against; cognitive-science work on expert routines (Chi et al. 1981/2014); 'What are tools anyway?' survey (Wang et al. 2024b) for the workflow-as-action framing.
contrasts_with: Synapse and other example-demonstration-in-context methods (Zheng et al. 2024; Fu et al. 2024) that augment with concrete full examples and entangle example-specific contexts — AWM contrasts by inducing abstract, reusable sub-routine workflows (less element-selection bias, better cross-task/website/domain generalization). SteP/HEAP (Sodhi et al. 2023) which rely on human-expert-written workflows — AWM induces workflows automatically without human supervision and still surpasses SteP. Fixed/training-based agents (BAGEL Murty et al. 2024; Fu et al. 2024) that integrate a fixed example set and lack robustness to context changes; non-adapting baselines (BrowserGym, MindAct) that solve each task independently without learning from past experience. Rule-based-only induction (AWM_rule) contrasted with LM-based abstract induction.
lineage: Group F (decision / memory / RL — experience-memory planners): a workflow-memory web agent that induces abstracted, reusable procedural routines from past trajectories and grows them online to guide future planning, in the lineage of ICL web/computer agents (ReAct -> MindAct/Synapse -> AWM) and LM library-/skill-learning (Voyager, TroVE, DreamCoder/LILO). Bridges retrieval-augmented prompting and continual experience/skill memory; distinct from concrete-trajectory CBR (Synapse) by its abstraction-to-workflow step.
